All original text is present, with zero-based original span markers <SPAN i>...</SPAN i>. For supported/opposed hypotheses cite all original evidence span indices for that decision, including independently operative redundant support and necessary governing language. For NotMentioned return an empty evidence list. Treat conditions and exceptions within scope, and distinguish limited permission from universal permission. Give a short public reason (at most 15 words per hypothesis), then report supplied skill IDs actually used. Skills are fallible reusable inspection procedures, not facts about this NDA or automatic verdicts. All skills are visible together; public hypothesis IDs describe applicability, not hidden context isolation. Do not execute further tools, invent citations or rewrite span indices. Return exactly the supplied JSON schema with all 17 original hypothesis keys. For each emit choice, spans, reason, used_skill_ids in that order. The common schema describes permitted values, not answers about this contract. Evidence candidates are fallible, not mandatory citations; make every final label and evidence decision yourself from the complete original contract. Work through the supplied public hypotheses. Each question contains its own complete applicable skill records and fallible source candidates. All 17 questions and the full contract remain visible together; a skill on a different question is not a condition that this question must satisfy. Independently inspect the entire source even when this question has no skills or candidates. A missing skill, an unestablished when condition, or a null relation_if_established never means NotMentioned. A non-null conditional relation is not a verdict about this contract. Check the complete condition and original hypothesis polarity yourself. Skill IDs reported for a question must come from that question's supplied records; an empty used_skill_ids list is always allowed. Possible list introductions are fallible layout suggestions, not proven legal dependencies or required citations. Decide every original label and final evidence set yourself.

{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>THIS CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) made this day of , (the “Effective Date”) by and between a corporation, and a corporation, (collectively, the “Parties” and each individually a “Party”).</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>The Parties are exploring the possibility of engaging in one or more mutually beneficial business relationships (collectively, the “Business Relationship”). </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>The Parties recognize that in the course of their discussions to further the Business Relationship, it will be necessary for each Party to disclose to the other certain Confidential Information (as defined below). </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>Each Party desires to set forth the terms that apply to such Confidential Information.</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the foregoing, of the promises and covenants set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties do hereby agree as follows:</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>1. The Parties shall </SPAN 6><SPAN 7>(i) use reasonable efforts to maintain the confidentiality of the information and materials, whether oral, written or in any form whatsoever, of the other that may be reasonably understood, from legends, the nature of such information itself and/or the circumstances of such information’s disclosure, to be confidential and/or proprietary thereto or to third parties to which either of them owes a duty of nondisclosure (collectively, “Confidential Information”); </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>(ii) take reasonable action in connection therewith, including without limitation at least the action that each takes to protect the confidentiality of its comparable proprietary assets; </SPAN 8><SPAN 9>(iii) to the extent within their respective possession and/or control, upon termination of this Agreement for any reason, immediately return to the provider thereof all Confidential Information not licensed or authorized to be used or enjoyed after termination or expiration hereof, and </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>(iv) with respect to any person to which disclosure is contemplated, require such person to execute an agreement providing for the treatment of Confidential Information set forth in clauses </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>(i) through </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>(iii). </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>The foregoing shall not require separate written agreements with employees and agents already subject to written agreements substantially conforming to the requirements of this Section nor with legal counsel, certified public accountants, or other professional advisers under a professional obligation to maintain the confidences of clients.</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>2. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the obligation of a person to protect the confidentiality of any information or materials shall terminate as to any information or materials which: </SPAN 14><SPAN 15>(i) are, or become, public knowledge through no act or failure to act of such person; </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>(ii) are publicly disclosed by the proprietor thereof; </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>(iii) are lawfully obtained without obligations of confidentiality by such person from a third party after reasonable inquiry regarding the authority of such third party to possess and divulge the same; </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>(iv) are independently developed by such person from sources or through persons that such person can demonstrate had no access to Confidential Information; or </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>(v) are lawfully known by such person at the time of disclosure other than by reason of discussions with or disclosures by the Parties.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>3. All Confidential Information delivered pursuant to this Agreement shall be and remain the property of the disclosing Party, and any documents containing or reflecting the Confidential Information, and all copies thereof, shall be promptly returned to the disclosing Party upon written request, or destroyed at the disclosing Party’s option. </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>Nothing herein shall be construed as granting or conferring any rights by license or otherwise, express or implied, regarding any idea made, conceived or acquired prior to or after the Effective Date, nor as granting any right with respect to the use or marketing of any product or service. </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>The Parties shall use the Confidential Information only for the Business Relationship. </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>The obligations of the Parties under this Agreement shall continue and survive the completion or abandonment of the Business Relationship and shall remain binding for a period of two (2) years from the Effective Date.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>4. As a violation by either Party of this Agreement could cause irreparable injury to the other Party and as there is no adequate remedy at law for such violation, the non-breaching Party may, in addition to any other remedies available to it at law or in equity, enjoin the breaching Party in a court of equity for violating or threatening to violate this Agreement. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>In the event either Party is required to enforce this Agreement through legal action, then it will be entitled to recover from the other Party all costs incurred thereby, including without limitation, reasonable attorney’s fees.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>5. Neither Party makes any representation or warranty with respect to any Confidential Information disclosed by it, nor shall either Party or any of their respective representatives have any liability hereunder with respect to the accuracy or completeness of any Confidential Information or the use thereof.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>6. Any provision of this Agreement held or determined by a court (or other legal authority) of competent jurisdiction to be illegal, invalid, or unenforceable in any jurisdiction shall be deemed separate, distinct and independent, and shall be ineffective to the extent of such holding or determination without </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>(i) invalidating the remaining provisions of this Agreement in that jurisdiction or </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>(ii) affecting the legality, validity or enforceability of such provision in any other jurisdiction.</SPAN 29>
<SPAN 30>7. Any notice required or permitted to be given hereunder shall be </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>(a) in writing, </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>(b) effective on the first business day following the date of receipt, and </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>(c) delivered by one of the following means: </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>(i) by personal delivery; </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>(ii) by prepaid, overnight package delivery or courier service; or </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>(iii) by the United States Postal Service, first class, certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid. </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>All notices given under this Agreement shall be addressed to the addresses stated at the outset of this Agreement, or to new or additional addresses as the Parties may be advised in writing.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>8. This Agreement is to be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the state of . </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>Neither Party shall be deemed to waive any of its rights, powers or remedies hereunder unless such waiver is in writing and signed by said Party. </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>This Agreement is binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their successor and assigns.</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>9. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement and understanding of the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, and is intended as the Parties’ final expression and complete and exclusive statement of the terms thereof, superseding all prior or contemporaneous agreements, representations, promises and understandings, whether written or oral. </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>Neither Party is to be bound by any pre-printed terms appearing in the other Party’s form documents, tariffs, purchase orders, quotations, acknowledgments, invoices, or other instruments. </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>This Agreement may be amended or modified only by an instrument in writing signed by both Parties.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized officers on the day and year first above written.</SPAN 44>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required upon termination of the agreement.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its triggering event. A duty triggered only by the discloser's request does not establish a termination-triggered duty; termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, or abandonment must itself activate the duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative return-or-destruction duty together with language linking it to termination or an equivalent end event.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, or the existence of dealings between the parties.
guidance.inspection: Treat a prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions are occurring as covering the fact of the agreement or negotiation, even when the restriction is framed as disclosure to the public or media rather than as secrecy of the document itself.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition and the text identifying the protected fact; retain any governing introduction needed to show that the listed fact is prohibited from disclosure.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that every covered disclosure mode is subject to an express identification mechanism, including any oral or non-written mode. A universal marking rule may use different procedures for written and oral disclosures.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite all clauses needed to cover each disclosure mode and its identification requirement; do not rely on one mode while another remains unconditional.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make any copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Find an express copying route, such as prior written consent, copies needed for authorized persons, or automatic backup creation acknowledged by the agreement. Permission may be conditional and need not be general.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite language expressly addressing copying, reproduction, or backup creation and the condition that authorizes it; access or disclosure permission alone is insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement expressly prohibits copying confidential information.
guidance.inspection: If copying is barred and the complete agreement provides no condition under which the receiving party may copy, the conditional-copy permission hypothesis is negated. A consent exception would instead be a permission circumstance.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify that no consent, operational-copy, backup, or other copying exception appears elsewhere.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.
